rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected-cluster disclosure at 29:2 names the shared evidence with 29:3 as 'the shared token... is a single word,' but the object actually shared is the triliteral root realized in two different binyanim (Qal here vs. Piel at 29:3) -- a root-level echo, not a word-level one.
rulings.grounds: Byte-tier splice from verse_map_oshb.json (programmatic, not hand-typed) of the row's own two forms: 29:2 token 'יִשְׂמַ֣ח' carries hiriq-yod, sheva-shin, patah-mem, NO dagesh; 29:3 token 'יְשַׂמַּ֣ח' carries sheva-yod, patah-shin, patah-mem PLUS U+05BC DAGESH OR MAPIQ on the mem. That dagesh is the Piel middle-radical doubling marker: 29:2 is Qal imperfect 3ms (intransitive, 'the people rejoice'), 29:3 is Piel imperfect 3ms (causative, 'brings his father joy') -- distinct binyanim of one root 'שמח', byte-confirmed. Consonant-only skeletons ARE identical ('ישמח'='ישמח', consonantal_index.json), matching the row's own observed_substrate_signals ('exact skeleton-tier match') -- but rejected_alternative calls the same object 'a single word,' overstating identity past what the byte tier supports. prov_device_inventory.json's own catchword_adjacency.count_object defines this class as 'adjacent-verse pairs sharing >=1 content token (skeleton tier...)' -- the campaign's own inventory names the object at skeleton tier, never word tier, which the row's phrasing outruns (SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE, TOOLKIT.md). Corroboration: LF's OWN supporting evidence for this same row independently derived the identical Qal/Piel byte fact ('the two pointed forms differ... so even the shared skeleton token is not a repeated identical form') without extending it to a challenge against the row's wording -- both primaries reached the same byte fact; only OL escalated it to a wording defect. Effect on the boundary call: none -- naming the object at root/cross-binyan level makes the cluster evidence thinner, not thicker, so the atomic verdict is reinforced, not threatened.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave edit to P12-030.rejected_alternative ONLY (seam-pair with P12-031 -- one edit class, apply to both rows per SEAM-PAIR CURES ARE ONE EDIT): replace 'the shared token (...) is a single word' with root-across-binyan phrasing aligned to the row's own observed_substrate_signals, e.g. 'the shared item is the root שמח at the skeleton tier only -- Qal יִשְׂמַ֣ח (oshb:Prov.29.2) here vs. Piel יְשַׂמַּ֣ח (oshb:Prov.29.3) there, not a repeated word-form.' Test the cure must pass: byte re-collation (collate.py) of both quoted forms must show the dagesh-in-mem presence/absence distinction disclosed, not elided; rejected_alternative and observed_substrate_signals must agree on object level (root/skeleton, never 'word') within the same row.

rulings.challenge_claim: The mirrored disclosure at 29:3 repeats the same object-level imprecision as 29:2: it calls the shared item with 29:2 'one shared word,' when the two are different binyan forms of one shared root, not one shared word-form.
rulings.grounds: Same byte-tier facts as P12-030's ruling (adjudicated as one defect, mirrored across the seam): Piel יְשַׂמַּ֣ח (29:3, dagesh U+05BC present on the mem) vs. Qal יִשְׂמַ֣ח (29:2, no dagesh) -- confirmed by direct codepoint inspection of tokens spliced from verse_map_oshb.json. Skeleton-tier identity ('ישמח') is real and is exactly what prov_device_inventory.json's catchword_adjacency actually counts. P12-031's own observed_substrate_signals already say 'exact-matches... at the skeleton tier' (correct, root-level), but rejected_alternative says 'one shared word... is not a chain' (overstates to word-identity). This is NOT a distinct defect from P12-030's -- it is the same object-naming imprecision applied to the mirror-image row of the same pair. Not a case of both primaries flagging the same row: LF supported both P12-030 and P12-031 without challenge, though LF's own P12-030 evidence independently surfaced the identical Qal/Piel fact without escalating it.
rulings.remedy: Same edit class as P12-030 (seam-pair, one cure applied twice): replace 'one shared word... is not a chain' with root-across-binyan phrasing, e.g. 'the shared item is the same root שמח at the skeleton tier only, not a repeated word-form (Piel יְשַׂמַּ֣ח here vs. Qal יִשְׂמַ֣ח at 29:2) -- not a chain.' Same test as P12-030: byte re-collation confirms the binyan distinction is disclosed; rejected_alternative aligned with observed_substrate_signals' existing root/skeleton-tier language.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row misdescribes its own verse's parallelism class: rationale and device_notes call Prov.29.14 non-antithetic and Synthetic, but rejected_alternative calls it 'its own antithesis' -- though the boundary verdict itself is independently correct.
rulings.grounds: Byte-tier text of Prov.29.14, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json: 'מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן'. This is a single participial clause (king judging) plus a consequence clause (throne established forever), with no vav-adversative conjunction and no second contrasted subject anywhere in the verse. This confirms the row's own rationale ('not a two-party antithesis') and device_notes ('Synthetic parallelism on royal justice and dynastic stability') are byte-accurate, and that rejected_alternative's clause 'the couplet here already completes its own antithesis' is a genuine internal contradiction: the verse has no antithetic structure to complete, by the row's own correct classification and by the clause-structure bytes themselves. The atomic/no-cluster boundary call is unaffected -- independent skeleton re-derivation (consonantal_index.json) confirms zero shared tokens between 29:14 and 29:13 or 29:15, matching both primaries' re-sweeps.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave edit to P12-042.rejected_alternative ONLY: drop 'antithesis' language and state the actual reason the 29:14/29:15 merge fails in terms consistent with the row's own synthetic classification, e.g. 'no catchword bridges the pair, and the verse already completes its own single-clause justice-to-permanence sequence.' Test the cure must pass: a terminology cross-check confirming rationale, device_notes, and rejected_alternative name the same parallelism class for the verse (no antithetic-class language attached to a verse device_notes calls Synthetic).
